main_topics.reason: The user came to understand a newly explained diagnosis and said they had not understood it at the appointment.
The user asked what they could do, requested more options to write down, and later said the practical guidance was useful.
The user described a pounding heart, dizziness, lightheadedness, and spotty vision when standing.
The user said they were scared their heart might be damaged and later reported feeling less panicked.
The user asked why POTS appeared after COVID despite previously being healthy and active.
The user directly asked whether POTS would be permanent and whether people get better.
The user said exertion with long COVID leads to crashes lasting days and expressed fear about exercise advice.
The user asked whether they should start medication and accepted a question to raise with their doctor.
The user asked what to do during episodes of heart racing and said the suggested steps were useful.
The user said prior advice to exercise had backfired and made them feel they were failing.

output.summary: The user wanted to understand a new POTS diagnosis after long COVID, including why it may have developed, whether it could improve, and ways to manage symptoms. The assistant explained the condition, discussed self-management and medication options, and addressed the user’s concern that exercise could trigger prolonged crashes; the user said they felt less panicked and understood that their heart was not broken.
